i thought it may be helpful to share ways we all save money. i don't know about you all, but as a family of 7 and with prices going up, we need to find ways to pinch pennies. everyone's lists will be different and that's perfectly fine. it is what makes us unique. so please no judgment.   1. we don't have a heat/air system. surely that has saved us something. though these days it is much harder to tell.2. we gather free firewood, by hand from people who need brush and trees taken out 3. we cook from scratch and rarely eat out. using basic ingredients, we cut out all of those prepackaged dead foods. which also keeps us healthy and far from a doctor. that's a bonus!4. we only use a dryer in bad weather. and once our dryer goes to dryer heaven, we have no intentions on replacing it. a clothesline is a good thing!5. we replaced our toilets with compost toilets built from pallets. the secret here is mulch. 6. we haven't bought toilet paper since before covid was a thing. we use cloth and rags. seeing as how we had a little one in cloth diapers, and they needed washed and hung on the line, it only made sense... same goes with feminine products!7. we attempt to grow and raise all of our food. some years are better than others, but every little bit counts. we also don't pay to have someone else do the animal processing. that happens here as a family.8. we have very few appliances other than refrigerator, freezer and washer. most of the lightbulbs in our home have been removed. we don't use a dishwasher, microwave, toaster, etc. we also don't have a television. we read instead.9. we make our own home care products. there is an upfront cost, but in the long run you save. we also make the majority of our herbal infusions, tinctures, syrups and salves.10. we keep a compost bin. also use deep bedding method for our poultry and keep a worm bin. any other extra kitchen scraps go to the pigs. 11. speaking of deep bedding, we had 10 tons of free wood chips brought in. the chickens work for us and scratch it up, turning it into a lovely compost for the garden. also used in the composting toilet.13. we shop second hand. buy used and save the difference! 14. we buy in bulk when possible. you can get basics at a much lower cost 15. we make our own entertainment. i cannot tell you the last time we went to a movie or concert. 15 years possibly? our friends think us odd that someone in their mid 30s wouldn't want to do what the world does. getting my hair done, or my nails. nah, i would much rather improve something on the homestead or learn a new skill.i could go on and on. these are just a few ways we save. i could also probably make just as large of a list of things that need improvement. but this is a journey. we may never fully get there. i would love to hear ways you save money during these hard times.
